Let’s break this down.  

An SCR’s surge current rating is usually given for a half-cycle duration at the rated frequency (here 50 Hz).  
At 50 Hz, one cycle = \( \frac{1}{50} \) s = 20 ms.  
Half-cycle = \( \frac{10}{50} \) ms = 10 ms.  

The surge current rating is based on the \( I^2 t \) (thermal energy) withstand capability of the device.  
For a given \( I^2 t \), if the time changes, the allowable current changes inversely with the square root of time ratio.  

Given:  
\( I_{\text{half-cycle}} = 3000 \text{ A} \)  
\( t_{\text{half-cycle}} = 10 \text{ ms} \)  
\( t_{\text{full-cycle}} = 20 \text{ ms} \)  

Using \( I^2 t = \text{constant} \):  
\[
I_{\text{full-cycle}}^2 \cdot t_{\text{full-cycle}} = I_{\text{half-cycle}}^2 \cdot t_{\text{half-cycle}}
\]  
\[
I_{\text{full-cycle}}^2 \cdot 20 = (3000)^2 \cdot 10
\]  
\[
I_{\text{full-cycle}}^2 = \frac{3000^2 \cdot 10}{20} = 3000^2 \cdot 0.5
\]  
\[
I_{\text{full-cycle}} = 3000 \cdot \sqrt{0.5} = 3000 \cdot 0.7071 \approx 2121.32 \text{ A}
\]  

This matches option (C).  

Final answer: (C)
